epics.title: REST/OpenAPI-to-MCP access and bounded credentials
epics.intent: Expose applicable application behavior to independent clients through standard MCP and ordinary application authority.
exit_criteria: Every exposed operation has equivalent domain authorization/entitlement decisions over REST, web and MCP.
A dated pinned protocol/SDK/client matrix records observed compatibility and explicit exclusions.
Current account/workspace state, revocation, proof challenges and failure semantics pass denied-path checks.
No customer agent governance inbox, hosted agent runtime, or invented future protocol is introduced.

tasks.objective: Choose a supported standard profile from primary sources at execution time and distinguish the existing AMSL subset from full interoperability.
instructions: Read the then-current official MCP specification and official Go SDK release/source; record dated specification URLs, exact revisions, transports and minimum Go version.
Compare public-client PKCE, confidential clients, metadata-document support, discovery, resource binding and redirect requirements with the pinned AMSL contract; classify supported, excluded or gap.
Define at least two independent target clients, their exact versions, synthetic test scripts and success/denial evidence format; do not infer qualification from package names.
Write a profile fixture test rejecting a missing version, unspecified client or silently enabled unsupported feature.
acceptance: Profile contains immutable references, explicit exclusions and resource/issuer model.
Profile fixture rejects unspecified protocol versions and unsupported enabled capabilities.
tasks.negative_test: Enable remote client metadata fetching without its SSRF contract; profile check must reject it.
risks: Proposed paths and commands require T1.2 contract freeze and stage-entry revalidation; they are not evidence of existing implementation.
